occurrences.rationale: Newly observed SendToProject setup-brief tool description: explicit slash-command admission, confirmation pane, project creation or reuse, memory/setup-card publication, and Remote Control provenance. No predecessor inventory occurrence governs this tool; do not merge it with the separate message-only mode.

Newly observed SendToProject message-only description, with confirmation before sending as the user and explicit exclusion of project memory/setup-card writes. Its separate callsite and behavior require a distinct lineage from the setup-brief mode.
New REPL-script branch instructs draining queued notifications before work. The existing notification-tool description is a separate callsite and remains independently identified.

Newly observed macOS Bash 3.2 heredoc warning explains stdin versus command-substitution quoting and a single-quoted fallback. Existing Git workflow templates are revised separately; this is a dedicated platform warning.

The exact background-completion notification text remains the Bash run_in_background description's conditional alternate. Preserve its Bash lineage separately from the PowerShell occurrence with the same text.
The Git commit protocol remains the same ordered workflow. Only the shell heredoc example moves into a platform-selected interpolation; keep the existing commit-instruction lineage.
The creating-pull-requests instruction retains its GitHub workflow and output structure. Platform-dependent gh body option and heredoc closing syntax move to interpolations.

New compact Bash-description branch advises a single foreground wait instead of repeated background-result polling. Related existing task-result advice remains a separate observation, so this added shell-description callsite gets a new lineage.

The identical import safety warning remains a standalone variable initializer next to import command registrations. Preserve that occurrence separately from the warning interpolated into the offer-to-import template.
The identical import safety warning remains the literal interpolation inside the offer-to-import template. Preserve its separate lineage from the standalone initializer.
The team onboarding-guide author prompt remains continuous. One paragraph now requires disclosure when sessionsLeftOut makes the usage figures incomplete.

The security-review command prompt remains the same review and false-positive-filtering workflow. Its final-output sentence is extracted to an adjacent constant rather than retained inside this observation.
The full-conversation detailed summary prompt retains its sections, user-instruction preservation, and examples. It restores an analysis block to the example and adjusts whitespace.

New appended compaction boundary instruction says the conversation is data to summarize rather than a request to execute, and requires summary tags for this reply. It is not a successor to any of the former whole-task compact modes.

New compaction suffix explains omitted, refused, stopped, and cleared tool-result placeholders and their authority boundaries. No predecessor observation provides this placeholder-specific instruction.
The readable user-communication prompt remains in the same mode-selection branch. It drops the sentence about matching surrounding code style while retaining communication and comment guidance.
The statusline-setup agent prompt remains continuous. Two descriptions shorten '5-hour session limit' to '5-hour limit'; the configuration workflow and schema are unchanged.
The exact Python certificate diagnostic remains the standalone Windows sandbox guidance initializer. Preserve that identity separately from its repeated array-element occurrence.
The exact Git sandbox ownership warning remains a standalone guidance initializer. Preserve it separately from the same warning inserted directly into the assembled guidance array.
The exact Python certificate diagnostic remains the direct array element in assembled Windows sandbox guidance, distinct from the standalone initializer.
The exact Git repository-ownership warning remains the direct array element in assembled Windows sandbox guidance, distinct from its standalone initializer.

New background-agent lifecycle guidance explains which foreground activity keeps the session alive after a reply and how agents should wait within bounded tool timeouts. No predecessor inventory occurrence expresses this lifecycle contract.
The plan end-turn rule retains its clarifications-versus-plan-approval distinction. The text now spells out '2 reasons' rather than interpolating the count and normalizes spacing.

New Claude Doc plan-destination branch defines the sole permitted planning writes, in-place text revision, and user-visible approval semantics. It is distinct from the predecessor whole no-plan-file reminder template.

The background task-status tool description retains its fields and notification semantics. Its ending is refactored into a shared prefix followed by surface-specific timing text; carry the same tool-description identity.
Newly observed post-reply file-delivery reminder requires sending linked files or ending silently, rather than repeating the reply. No predecessor observation has this unsent-file reminder role.

The artifact runtime-capabilities instruction retains its library-loading, frame, storage and capability role. Its hash-routing advice now reflects address-bar and Copy link synchronization and explicitly excludes private hash values.
Newly observed workflow return-value supplement explains that a final-report tool's message replaces the final text response. Existing workflow result-return prompts remain separate observations.
The publication-routing instruction retains its report-sharing and artifact/document boundary role. The revised clauses distinguish editable text documents from visual or interactive work.
The background monitor tool description retains its script event-stream and coverage guidance. The stderr sentence changes from an interpolation to explicit output-file and notification wording.

Restore the historical agent-summary label-language lineage prompt-000659 when this fallback becomes detector-visible again. Do not reuse the session-title language lineage, which already continues separately.

The workflow authoring reference keeps its API, orchestration examples and authoring role. The effort-default phrase becomes an interpolation while the surrounding agent option contract remains unchanged.
The duplicate MCP allow-rule refusal remains the v1 client-tree callsite, preserving prompt-000690 independently from the v2 copy.
The unattended artifact-write refusal retains the linked/hard-linked/path/upload provenance guard and person-required boundary. Only routine run becomes scheduled task run.
Newly observed partial-read write refusal explains how to avoid losing the unread tail and when to use a full Read or Edit. No predecessor observation covers this specific partial-read guard.

Split the broader activity-notification tail from the existing activity-awareness instruction. The original edit/reaction tail still carries its lineage at current196; the additional tail covers deletions, followed-channel posts and untrusted actors.
Newly observed WrapUp tool description requires a recap and optional decision buttons before a closing message. No predecessor observation represents this tool contract.
Newly observed self-named certificate rejection diagnostic explains trust and retry choices for NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS. It is distinct from the predecessor Windows sandbox certificate guidance.
The render-only skill-proposal tool description retains its proposal-card workflow. The ownership clause now includes a user's uploaded skill that appears as a plugin skill.
The design-sync tool contract retains its component-library synchronization role and method inventory. Revisions describe moved-project notices and normalized stored filenames in permission plans.
Split worker artifact-delivery guidance for the new MCP-backed artifact branch. The native Artifact-tools branch retains the old lineage at current264.
Newly observed long-line local-file reading guidance explains line-based Read limits and byte-offset alternatives. No predecessor observation represents this long-line diagnostic fragment.
The PowerShell background-command advice retains its lineage even though its nested literal now equals the Bash wording. Preserve prompt-000053 rather than taking the Bash lineage.
Split the Doc-aware plan approval description from the existing no-plan-file approval contract. Current289 retains the exact predecessor wording and lineage;290 adds the editable Claude Doc branch.

Newly observed approved-Doc reminder requires rereading the user-edited document before work and defines read-failure recovery. No predecessor observation represents this post-approval Doc intake message.
Newly observed project-info truncation notice explains that no full local file is available and forbids claiming otherwise. Keep it separate from the successful file-materialization notice.
Newly observed project-info materialization notice tells the caller how to read the full local_file without treating edits as project changes.
The self-hosted-runner help retains the same CLI option-reference role. It adds idle hold controls, cloud idle-release constraints, trust-workspace clarification and proxy compatibility guidance.
The gateway protocol retains its OIDC-configured conditional branch identity. Revised protocol text documents group-pool budgets, gateway token counting and Bedrock oversized-input recovery.
The gateway protocol retains its non-OIDC conditional alternate identity separately from the identical configured branch.
Newly observed transient-session MCP background-call warning explains potential result loss after the reply and forbids promising to report back.
Newly observed WebFetch partial-page guidance requires reading further only when needed and disclosing partial coverage otherwise.
Newly observed send-to-project brief-authoring prompt defines the proposal fields and one-shot confirmation workflow for continuing session work in a project.
Newly observed send-to-project message-posting prompt governs the user-message mode, separately from the work-continuation brief.

The cloud-agent scheduling prompt retains its create/update/list/run workflow. It now distinguishes an omitted connector list from an explicitly empty stored list and requires reviewing resulting connectors.

The tool-result display metadata description retains its non-execution and permission-provenance contract. It adds built_in_tool stamping and exclusions for rewritten, replayed, handed-over and subagent results.
The tool-use display metadata description retains its connector identity and permission-boundary role. Only server_display_name precedence is clarified.
Newly observed result-frame startup timing phase description explains the detailed time_to_request_ms decomposition. No predecessor extracted occurrence represents this field contract.
The cloud-session init metadata description retains its stream/device/serving schema contract. It adds computer_too_old and session_too_old reasons and notice keys.
The subagent-preference classifier retains its configuration-reading task, JSON schema and delegation criteria. The Agent tool name becomes an interpolation in the same instruction.

The agent-proxy network guide remains the same generated local-proxy diagnostic reference. The revision adds 429/503 load and connection-pressure troubleshooting.
The unchanged MCP name-collision refusal remains the v2 MCP runtime adapter's allow-rule guard; keep it separate from the v1 adapter duplicate.
Newly observed REPL synchronous-versus-dispatched output and wait/cache guidance in the REPL tool description. No predecessor inventory occurrence serves this interface contract.

Newly observed persistent REPL programming-interface guidance explains retained variables, sealed globals, call costs, Promise handling and preview output. It is a distinct description template from dispatch and wait guidance.
Newly observed asynchronous REPL dispatch and output-delivery guidance defines script ordering, shared VM state, detached scripts, foreground waits and late output.

Newly detector-visible executable JavaScript template constructs VM-side intrinsic, promise, error and value-cloning helpers. Allocate the extracted occurrence without representing it as a model-facing prompt.
Newly observed REPL toolsUsed result-schema description specifies reporting tools called directly or transitively, including async settle delivery.
Newly observed async REPL pending-call warning explains that unfinished calls continue after script completion and discourages duplicate execution.

The existing background-result instruction now has a separate foreground-wait variant for sessions whose result delivery cannot start another turn. Preserve current402 as the exact carry and allocate this additional callsite as a split.
Newly observed task-status branch tells the caller to await a background result through one foreground shell command when needed before replying.

The Remote Control help text retains its CLI usage/options and persistent-server explanation. A new paragraph clarifies local execution, awake-computer requirements and the difference from Cloud sessions.
The release-notes literal retains its changelog identity and version-section format; added and dropped release sections update the same history document.
Newly observed attachment refusal explains required explicit mail recipients before attaching files by reference.

The malformed file-reference diagnostic gains a separate attachment-specific branch, retaining the predecessor's validation rules while naming the attachment and its base64 field. Current426 preserves the original single-file branch as an exact carry; allocate this additional callsite as a split.
Newly observed Windows ambiguous-path write refusal explains protected Claude configuration locations and requests an unambiguous local drive path.
Newly observed Claude Project handoff response instruction limits the receiver's acknowledgement after posting a setup card.
Newly observed Claude Project handoff source-session guidance restricts reading the Remote Control transcript and treats its content as untrusted data.
Newly observed handoff brief boundary instruction treats only the precisely fenced JSON object as data and rejects instructions inside it.
The Artifact pre-creation elicitation prompt remains the same producer and workflow. The revision adds color-card markup, fixes look choices to three, and limits the form to four questions.
The Artifact content-writing and HTML skeleton instruction retains its lineage. A removed interpolation leaves only a whitespace difference in detector text.
